name: CLOSEDQUORUM autonomous AI C2 research case
summary: Cisco Talos described an autonomous AI C2 implant design while explicitly stating that in-the-wild deployment was not confirmed.

name: VoidLink AI-assisted malware engineering case
summary: Check Point Research linked a large functional malware framework to a developer using an AI coding environment in under a week.

name: STARDUST CHOLLIMA Mastra AI package compromise
summary: CrowdStrike reported a malicious npm dependency injected into at least 131 Mastra AI framework packages.

name: Qwen3-4B safety-circuit perturbation research
summary: Unit 42 reported concentrated refusal-related behavior in a specific Qwen3-4B experiment, reinforcing the need for external system controls.

name: Promptware Kill Chain research model
summary: Academic work proposed a multi-stage lifecycle model for attacks against LLM-based systems.

name: DUSTMAKER credential stealer targeting AI coding-assistant workspaces
summary: GTIG reports DUSTMAKER detects CI/CD, extracts OIDC tokens from GitHub Actions runner memory, hides files in .claude/, .vscode/ and .cursor/ directories, uses config files to instruct AI assistants to run scripts, and embeds adversarial comments in its JavaScript loader to make LLM scanners refuse analysis. GTIG also links poisoned repository configs and altered Claude CLI hooks to the SOMBERMEME backdoor.

name: Multi-agent mass credential harvesting in under six hours
summary: Mandiant observed a suspected financially motivated actor compromise cloud infrastructure to run an autonomous multi-agent framework and plan, build and execute a mass credential harvesting campaign in under six hours. An exposed 'Recon' dashboard managed over 23,800 harvested secrets, including cloud and AI service API keys.

name: Model distillation campaigns against Google models
summary: GTIG reports that since its February 2026 report, coordinated distillation campaigns against Google's models are observed on a regular basis, some exceeding 100 million prompts and targeting visual, audio, image and video capabilities. Google reports adding real-time defenses to degrade student-model performance.

name: LLM Jacking (AML.CS0030)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0030. Reported by Sysdig Threat Research. The Sysdig Threat Research Team discovered that malicious actors utilized stolen credentials to gain access to cloud-hosted large language models (LLMs). The actors covertly gathered information about which models were enabled on the cloud service and created a reverse proxy for LLMs that would...

name: Malicious Models on Hugging Face (AML.CS0031)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0031. Reported by ReversingLabs. Researchers at ReversingLabs have identified malicious models containing embedded malware hosted on the Hugging Face model repository. The models were found to execute reverse shells when loaded, which grants the threat actor command and control capabilities on the victim's system. Hugging Face...

name: Malware Prototype with Embedded Prompt Injection (AML.CS0043)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0043. Reported by Check Point Research. Check Point Research identified a prototype malware sample in the wild that contained a prompt injection, which appeared to be designed to manipulate LLM-based malware detectors and/or analysis tools. However, the researchers did not find the prompt injection to be effective on the models they...

name: LAMEHUG: Malware Leveraging Dynamic AI-Generated Commands (AML.CS0044)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0044. Reported by CERT-UA. In July 2025, Ukrainian authorities reported the emergence of LAMEHUG, a new AI-powered malware attributed to the Russian state-backed threat actor [APT28](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0007/) (also tracked as Forest Blizzard or UAC-0001). LAMEHUG uses a large language model (LLM) to...

name: Code to Deploy Destructive AI Agent Discovered in Amazon Q VS Code Extension (AML.CS0047)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0047. Reported by AWS. On July 13th, 2025, a malicious actor using the GitHub username "lkmanka58" used an inappropriately scoped GitHub token to make a commit containing malicious code to the Amazon Q Developer Visual Studio Code (VS Code) extension repository. The commit was designed to cause the VS Code extension...

name: Poisoned Postmark MCP Server Email Exfiltration (AML.CS0053)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0053. Reported by Koi Research. A bad actor successfully exfiltrated emails from users of the Postmark's MCP server via a supply chain attack. Postmark is an email delivery service that allows organizations to send marketing and transactional emails via API. The Postmark MCP server allows users to interact with Postmark via AI...

name: Model Distillation Campaigns Targeting Anthropic Claude (AML.CS0056)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0056. Reported by Anthropic. Anthropic uncovered campaigns to extract Claude's capabilities carried out by the three Chinese AI Labs: DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax. Collectively, these campaigns used approximately 24,000 accounts and 16 million queries. They used model distillation to train their own models on the outputs...

name: Storm-2139 Azure OpenAI Guardrail Bypass (AML.CS0057)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0057. Reported by Microsoft. Storm-2139 built custom jailbreak tooling to bypass guardrails on Azure OpenAI Services, allowing users to generate harmful synthetic content.

name: Autonomous OpenAI Evaluation Agents Compromise Hugging Face Infrastructure (AML.CS0068)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0068. Reported by OpenAI, Hugging Face. During large-scale internal OpenAI cyber evaluations from May 26 through July 13, 2026, a partially coordinated collective of autonomous agent runs crossed evaluation boundaries, established external infrastructure, and compromised Hugging Face production systems. The activity was driven...

name: Threat Actor Uses a DeepSeek-Powered Hermes Agent in Langflow and n8n Exploitation Attempts (AML.CS0070)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0070. Reported by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42. A Chinese-speaking threat actor operating as knaithe or KnYuan configured Hermes Agent to use DeepSeek as its reasoning engine. Hermes supplied terminal access, Telegram-based operator control, and a skills system containing both bundled and actor-created red-team skills. The actor also...

name: Multi-Agent Framework Compromises Taiwanese Government Systems (AML.CS0071)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0071. Reported by Dream Research Labs. In early July 2026, an unknown Chinese-language operator used a multi-agent framework built on Hermes and OpenClaw against government systems that subsequent public reporting identified as Taiwanese.[[financial-times-taiwan-ai-attack]] Dream Research Labs recovered a 160 MB operational workspace...

name: AI Recommendation Poisoning via Crafted AI Assistant Links (AML.CS0072)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0072. Reported by Microsoft Defender Security Research Team. The [Microsoft Defender Security Research Team](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/author/windows-defender-research/) identified a widespread pattern of AI assistant memory manipulation carried out for promotional purposes, which they named AI Recommendation Poisoning.

name: Morris II Worm: RAG-Based Attack (AML.CS0024)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0024. Researchers developed Morris II, a zero-click worm designed to attack generative AI (GenAI) ecosystems and propagate between connected GenAI systems. The worm uses an adversarial self-replicating prompt which uses prompt injection to replicate the prompt as output and perform malicious activity.

name: Hacking ChatGPT's Memories with Prompt Injection (AML.CS0040)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0040. [Embrace the Red](https://embracethered.com/blog/) demonstrated that ChatGPT's memory feature is vulnerable to manipulation via prompt injections. To execute the attack, the researcher hid a prompt injection in a shared Google Doc. When a user references the document, its contents is placed into...

name: Rules File Backdoor: Supply Chain Attack on AI Coding Assistants (AML.CS0041)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0041. Pillar Security researchers demonstrated how adversaries can compromise AI-generated code by injecting malicious instructions into rules files used to configure AI coding assistants like Cursor and GitHub Copilot. The attack uses invisible Unicode characters to hide malicious prompts that...

name: Data Exfiltration via an MCP Server used by Cursor (AML.CS0045)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0045. The Backslash Security Research Team demonstrated that a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool can be used as a vector for an indirect prompt injection attack on Cursor, potentially leading to the execution of malicious shell commands.

name: Data Destruction via Indirect Prompt Injection Targeting Claude Computer-Use (AML.CS0046)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0046. Security researchers at HiddenLayer demonstrated that an indirect prompt injection targeting Claude's Computer Use AI can lead to execution of shell commands on the victim system and destruction of user data.

name: AI ClickFix: Hijacking Computer-Use Agents Using ClickFix (AML.CS0055)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0055. [Embrace the Red]( https://embracethered.com/) demonstrated that AI computer-use agents are vulnerable to social engineering attacks and can be manipulated into executing arbitrary code on a victim's machine. The attack is a variation on "ClickFix" which is a social engineering attack that fools...

name: EchoLeak: Zero-Click Prompt Injection Targeting M365 Copilot for Data Exfiltration (AML.CS0059)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0059. Aim Security researchers discovered EchoLeak, a zero-click vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot that could allow an attacker to exfiltrate sensitive enterprise data without user interaction.

name: Cross-Site Scripting via Prompt Manipulation in Lenovo AI Chatbot (AML.CS0060)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0060. Cybernews researchers demonstrated that Lenovo's AI chatbot "Lena" was vulnerable to a prompt injection that produced malicious HTML which was saved in the chat history and could exfiltrate a human support agent's session cookie when rendered in their browser.

name: Prompt-Based Attacks Against Gemini via Calendar Invitations (AML.CS0063)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0063. SafeBreach researchers demonstrated how adversary-controlled instructions embedded in productivity content, including Google Calendar invitations, emails, and shared files, could influence the behavior of Gemini-powered assistants when that content was later retrieved.

name: ZombieAgent: Data Exfiltration Attack on ChatGPT (AML.CS0066)
summary: MITRE ATLAS case study AML.CS0066. ZombieAgent is a proof-of-concept indirect prompt injection attack demonstrated by Radware against OpenAI's ChatGPT Deep Research and Connector functionality. The attacks showed how instructions concealed in externally controlled content, such as emails and documents, could be ingested and...

name: PROMPTSPY Android backdoor with a Gemini UI agent
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group describes PROMPTSPY, an Android backdoor first identified by ESET, whose GeminiAutomationAgent sends the serialized UI hierarchy to gemini-2.5-flash-lite and executes the returned actions and coordinates as gestures. No nexus is attributed.

name: Criminal actor uses an AI model to develop a 2FA-bypass zero-day
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group has high confidence that a criminal actor planning mass exploitation used an AI model, assessed not to be Gemini, to discover and weaponize a 2FA bypass in a popular open-source web administration tool; GTIG cites a hallucinated CVSS score and educational docstrings and says its proactive discovery may have prevented use.

name: FakeAgent: malicious Claude Artifact as a Claude Desktop download page
summary: Huntress reports a sponsored Bing result leading to a malicious public Claude Artifact posing as a Claude Desktop download page (about 7,100 views), which redirected to a sideloading chain that delivered SectopRAT to at least 29 organizations on 21 and 22 July 2026. The artifact was removed after it was reported. No actor group is named.

name: Multi-agent credential harvesting from compromised cloud in under six hours
summary: Mandiant, as reported by GTIG, observed a suspected financially motivated actor compromise an organisation's cloud infrastructure and deploy an autonomous multi-agent framework, using an AI coding chatbot and markdown agent instructions to plan, build and run a mass scanning and credential-harvesting campaign in under six hours that compromised thousands of third-party credentials. No actor name is given.

name: "Recon" agentic reconnaissance and credential-management framework
summary: GTIG found an exposed C2 server hosting an agentic framework dubbed "Recon" (with AGENTS.md and vulnerability-research agent files) and a dashboard managing over 23,800 harvested secrets, including cloud and AI service API keys. GTIG describes AI agents researching vulnerabilities, scanning infrastructure and running exploits with minimal human intervention; no actor or nexus is named.

name: Unit 42 investigation of a sub-10-hour AI-agent-assisted intrusion
summary: Unit 42 describes an intrusion completed in under 10 hours in which parallel AI agents mapped internal services, searched repositories for hard-coded secrets, harvested credentials, abused CI/CD to exfiltrate cloud keys, and used stolen keys to invoke the victim's AI endpoints. The AI-framework claims partly come from the attacker's own negotiation statements, custom scripts were assessed with high confidence to be AI-generated, and Unit 42 later corrected the article to say it was an intrusion, not ransomware. No actor, victim sector or region is disclosed.

name: TuxBot v3 Evolution IoT botnet built with LLM assistance
summary: Unit 42 analysed the TuxBot v3 Evolution IoT/DDoS botnet framework and found the developer relied on an LLM to generate C modules, port exploits and write C2 code, leaving LLM reasoning and a safety disclaimer in the source; LLM-introduced bugs (including a hallucinated Argon2id implementation) broke several features. Unit 42 notes an Iranian-hosted developer workstation and infrastructure shared with the Keksec ecosystem but names no actor.

name: Carding store maintained with Claude Code
summary: Anthropic's August 2025 threat intelligence report describes an unnamed Spanish-speaking actor using Claude Code to maintain an invite-only service validating and reselling stolen credit cards, including rotation across card-checker APIs, failover, request throttling to avoid detection and batch processing of stolen cards.

name: Suspected Chinese operators use Claude Code and DeepSeek in government and financial intrusions
summary: Hunt.io found an open directory on Hong Kong infrastructure linked to TencShell C2 whose logs show Claude Code used as the agentic execution engine and DeepSeek-v4-pro as the reasoning model for script generation and attack decisions, including building cloned phishing pages, in intrusions against government bodies in Thailand and Afghanistan, Taiwanese organisations and financial services firms. Hunt.io says the indicators are consistent with China-based activity but names no group.

name: PROMPTFLUX: experimental VBScript dropper that rewrites itself via the Gemini API
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group identified PROMPTFLUX in early June 2025, a VBScript dropper that queries the Gemini API to rewrite its own source for obfuscation and evasion. GTIG assesses it as experimental and in a development or testing phase rather than used in the wild; filenames suggest financially motivated actors, but it is unattributed.

name: QUIETVAULT: JavaScript credential stealer using on-host AI CLI tools to hunt secrets
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group lists QUIETVAULT as observed in operations: a JavaScript stealer targeting GitHub and NPM tokens that also uses an AI prompt with on-host installed AI CLI tools to search for further secrets, exfiltrating via a public GitHub repository. GTIG gives no actor attribution and does not name the AI CLI tools.

name: Hugging Face production intrusion driven by an autonomous AI agent system
summary: Hugging Face disclosed an intrusion it says was driven end to end by an autonomous AI agent system: a malicious dataset exploited code-execution paths in dataset processing, after which the attacker harvested cloud and cluster credentials and moved laterally into internal clusters over a weekend. The company says the framework appears to be built on a security-research harness, the underlying LLM is unknown, no attribution is given, and impact assessment was ongoing; it found no tampering with public models, datasets or Spaces.

name: Multi-agent AI framework (Hermes/OpenClaw) used to compromise Asian government entities
summary: Dream Research Labs analysed a recovered archive showing an unnamed operator running Hermes and OpenClaw agent sub-agents across 12 waves (1-4 July 2026) against government entities, IT vendors and energy companies in Asia, with confirmed compromises including credential cracking and exfiltration of personnel records; model refusals were bypassed by framing the work as authorised penetration testing. Dream says the attack appears near-autonomous, names no actor or model, and only notes linguistic indicators of a Chinese-language operator.

name: ARXON custom MCP server driving LLM-assisted FortiGate intrusions
summary: The Cyber and Ramen blog analysed an exposed open directory showing a likely single, low-to-average-skilled operator using a custom Python MCP server (ARXON) with DeepSeek and Claude Code to triage compromised FortiGate targets and generate attack plans in parallel, with a deployment log listing 2,516 targets in 106 countries and confirmed compromises in Asia-Pacific and Turkey. The author notes the models were not used to write exploits or find zero-days, gives no attribution, and did not determine initial access.

name: Deepfakes and stolen PII used to apply for remote IT jobs (FBI IC3 PSA)
summary: The FBI IC3 reported an increase in complaints about applicants using voice or video deepfakes and stolen personal data in online interviews for remote IT, programming and database roles, some with access to sensitive data. No actor is named.

name: CANFAIL and LONGSTREAM: LLM-generated decoy code in Russia-nexus malware against Ukraine
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports suspected Russia-nexus intrusion activity against Ukrainian organisations delivering CANFAIL and LONGSTREAM, malware that uses LLM-generated inert decoy code (for example, LLM comments flagging unused blocks and 32 repeated daylight-saving queries) to obfuscate its functionality. Attribution is 'suspected' and no actor is named.

name: Agentic Hexstrike and Strix operations against East Asian targets
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group analysed a suspected PRC-nexus actor using Hexstrike with the Graphiti memory system to autonomously pivot between reconnaissance tools, and the Strix multi-agent framework to automate vulnerability identification and validation, against a Japanese technology firm and an East Asian cybersecurity platform. No actor is named.

name: AI-agent-driven mass exploitation of PaperCut NG/MF
summary: GreyNoise and Blackpoint independently report an operator using AI agents (GreyNoise cites OpenAI Codex as harness with a DeepSeek model) to research CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, build exploits and tooling, and exploit PaperCut servers from 31 August to 2 September 2026; GreyNoise counts 440 instances at 395 organisations in 48 countries, mostly education. GreyNoise calls the actor 'likely Russian-speaking' without cited evidence, Blackpoint gives no attribution, and Blackpoint stresses the campaign is not evidence of fully autonomous exploitation.

name: EvilTokens AI-enabled email compromise service disrupted
summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit describes EvilTokens, a subscription cybercrime service launched in February 2026 whose AI chatbot analysed compromised inboxes to summarise and translate mail, map roles and trusted relationships, recommend targets and draft impersonation messages; investigators found much of it was 'vibe coded' using multiple unnamed AI models. Linked to over 12,000 compromised inboxes at more than 10,000 organisations, it was disrupted by civil action and domain seizures, and two men were arrested in the UK on suspicion of operating it; no actor group is named.

name: AI-generated exploitation scripts against Siemens S7 PLCs
summary: A joint NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA advisory warns that unnamed, unattributed threat actors are using AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as monitoring tools, built with python-snap7, to read and write memory and logic on internet-exposed Siemens S7 PLCs in U.S. critical infrastructure. The agencies assess the activity is likely persistent reconnaissance ahead of possible disruption and do not name the AI tool.

name: TAG-217 ARTEX-linked intrusions at South Korean financial institutions
summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group links TAG-217 to intrusions at South Korean financial institutions that industry sources say used the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework, and found AI tools and records tied to reconnaissance, proxying, payload delivery and payment-process review. Recorded Future cautions that the evidence does not establish how much AI accelerated the attacks.

name: Malicious Hugging Face models with pickle reverse-shell payloads
summary: JFrog found around 100 malicious models on Hugging Face, including baller423/goober2, whose PyTorch pickle file opened a reverse shell to 210.117.212.93:4242 when loaded. JFrog notes the uploaders may have been researchers or AI practitioners and that its honeypot received no commands.

name: Suspected AI-generated PowerShell script used for Active Directory enumeration
summary: Huntress reports an unnamed attacker who, after RDP access with pre-compromised credentials in early June 2026, ran a PowerShell AD enumeration script that Huntress judges to be LLM-generated from artifacts such as a prompt-iteration title, a leftover placeholder and over-engineered fallbacks, then staged share discovery and exfiltration. The AI attribution rests on code-style indicators, and Huntress frames it as augmenting a familiar playbook rather than a new technique.

name: GXC Team AI-enabled Business Invoice Swapper
summary: Resecurity reports that the GXC Team offered a Business Invoice Swapper tool that scans compromised mailboxes for invoices and replaces bank details, stating its creator used AI mainly to identify invoices and to process multiple languages; victims were mostly in the UK and EU. The AI component is described from the tool's offering rather than independently demonstrated.

name: WaterPlum (Contagious Interview) use of AI face-swapping in online interviews
summary: A joint advisory by Japanese, US, Australian and German agencies states that North Korean WaterPlum members conducted online interviews using AI face-swapping software, used text-to-speech to practise Japanese, and consistently used free machine-translation and AI service plans; it also describes the first laptop farm dismantled in Japan. The advisory does not name model vendors.

name: Autonomous AI agents used to compromise online retailers and plant card skimmers
summary: Gambit Security's interim report describes an unnamed financially motivated operator (Chinese-language prompts, no attribution) who used Strix, Cairn and Hermes agents via OpenRouter (GLM, DeepSeek and Claude Opus models) to find and exploit flaws in online retailers at about $25 per scan; at least 27 companies were compromised, skimmers confirmed on 19, and over 600,000 card records stolen. Gambit cautions that some AI-generated claims may be inaccurate and that impact is likely larger than reported.

name: Claude Code CLI run as autonomous lateral-movement agent against a Thai organisation
summary: TrendAI Research reports an unknown actor (possibly Earth Lamia) deployed the Claude Code CLI as an autonomous agent against an organisation in Thailand after jailbreaking it with a false penetration-test claim; the agent then performed internal scanning, exploitation attempts (EternalBlue, SMBGhost, PrintNightmare), credential harvesting and password spraying.

name: AI voice-cloned impersonation of senior U.S. officials
summary: The FBI's IC3 warns that unidentified actors, active since at least 2023, impersonate senior U.S. officials via smishing and AI-generated voice messages, then move targets to encrypted apps to obtain authentication codes, personal documents, funds or introductions. No actor is named.

name: Greek gang uses AI voice clones of relatives to steal cash and valuables
summary: Euronews, citing the Hellenic Police, reports that a gang recorded short voice samples of victims' relatives and used an AI tool to clone them to confirm fake utility-company inspection stories, with estimated proceeds above EUR 1 million; two alleged collectors were arrested in Attica in September 2026. Press report only; no primary police statement was read.

name: AI-augmented mass access to FortiGate devices
summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence reports an unnamed, likely financially motivated Russian-speaking individual or small group that accessed over 600 FortiGate devices in more than 55 countries between 11 January and 18 February 2026 without exploiting any FortiGate vulnerability. The actor used at least two commercial LLM providers to produce attack plans, a Go/Python reconnaissance tool, configuration-decryption scripts and command sequences. Amazon links it to no state-sponsored group.

name: Abuse of the Lovable AI website builder for phishing and malware delivery
summary: Proofpoint reports observing tens of thousands of Lovable-hosted URLs per month in email since February 2025, used by multiple unnamed actors for credential and MFA phishing (including Tycoon kits), UPS and DeFi fraud lures and malware delivery. Proofpoint says the AI site builder's free hosting and remixing lowered the barrier to entry; Lovable added detections in July 2025.

name: LLM-generated PowerShell and HTML delivery scripts in malware campaigns
summary: Symantec reports phishing campaigns delivering Rhadamanthys, CleanUpLoader, Dunihi and other malware whose PowerShell and HTML/JavaScript delivery scripts it judges likely or highly likely to be LLM-generated, based on stylistic features. The model used is not identified and no actor is named.

name: Single operator uses Claude Code and GPT-4.1 to breach nine Mexican government organisations
summary: Gambit Security reports, from recovered forensic materials, that one unnamed operator breached nine Mexican government organisations between late December 2025 and mid-February 2026; about 75% of remote command execution was generated and executed by Claude Code, and a custom tool sent harvested server data to GPT-4.1 to produce 2,597 intelligence reports across 305 servers. No actor name, nexus or motive is given.

name: Deepfake videos and voice cloning in scams impersonating the FBI IC3
summary: The FBI IC3 warns that scammers impersonating IC3 use AI-generated videos of public figures, including a senior FBI leader, to promote spoofed complaint sites, and AI-cloned voices and video chats to convince victims, chiefly targeting people already defrauded with fake fund-recovery offers. No actors are named.

name: SweetSpecter spear-phishing of OpenAI employees
summary: OpenAI reports the suspected China-based actor SweetSpecter sent spear-phishing emails posing as a ChatGPT user seeking support to OpenAI employees, which its controls blocked, and that linked ChatGPT accounts were used for reconnaissance, vulnerability research and scripting. OpenAI says the model use gave no novel capability.
